own_solution.law: Kinetic theory of an ideal gas: v_rms = sqrt(3 R T / M)

notes: Base: v_rms = sqrt(3*8.314*400/0.032) = sqrt(311775) = 558.37 m/s. Heated to 500 K: sqrt(3*8.314*500/0.032) = sqrt(389718.75) = 624.27 m/s. The amount n = 2 mol belongs to the gas and appears in p V = n R T and in the total mass n M, but cancels from v_rms = sqrt(3 p V / (n M)), so C. The metal block and the empty oven in another room have no physical path to the gas (D). Variant sets: T22C5/T9BED both state 2 mol (wording differs only); TB60B/T2519/T9BF3/T0A89 all state 100 K and differ only in what is heated. T2519 adds 'held in a closed rigid container', which does not alter v_rms (depends only on T and M), so it is still a 100 K rise to 500 K; this extra clause is a slight non-minimality relative to T0A89 but harmless. Interpreted 'raises the temperature by 100 K' as the gas then being at 500 K in equilibrium when measured.
